phase1.intro:
This lesson stocks the shelves — a tour of the actual controls a customer can touch.

Where should we start?

topics.buttonText: How do TextField, TextArea, and prompt text work?
dialogue: TextField takes a single line of typed input; TextArea takes several. Both support `setPromptText("...")` — [[key:prompt text is a hint, not a value]]; `getText()` on an untouched field returns an empty string, not the prompt.

stickyNote.flavor: 💬 prompt text is a visual hint, not a real value
stickyNote.definition: TextField (one line) and TextArea (multiple lines) both support setPromptText() as a placeholder hint — getText() returns empty, not the prompt.

topics.buttonText: Why do RadioButtons need a ToggleGroup?
dialogue: CheckBox is a simple on/off toggle via `setSelected()`. RadioButton is trickier — [[warn:radio buttons only become mutually exclusive once you assign them to the same ToggleGroup]]; skip that and a user could select three "exclusive" options at once.

stickyNote.flavor: ☑️ radio buttons need a shared ToggleGroup to be exclusive
stickyNote.definition: CheckBox toggles independently via setSelected(). RadioButtons only become mutually exclusive when assigned to the same ToggleGroup.

topics.buttonText: What about ComboBox, ListView, Slider, and Tooltip?
dialogue: ComboBox and ListView both hold a collection (`getItems().addAll(...)`), but ComboBox collapses to one row until clicked while ListView shows several rows scrollable. Slider and ProgressBar represent a value along a range. Tooltip attaches to another control with `setTooltip()`, appearing only on hover.

stickyNote.definition: ComboBox (collapsed dropdown) and ListView (scrollable rows) both hold collections. Slider/ProgressBar show a value along a range. Tooltip appears on hover.

phase1.output: (Window appears with all controls: Label, Button, TextField, TextArea, CheckBox, RadioButtons, ComboBox, ListView, Slider, ProgressBar, etc.)
phase1.openingDialogue: This lesson stocks the shelves — TextField, CheckBox, RadioButton, ComboBox, and more, none wired up to do anything yet. 📋

phase2.explanation:
[[warn:the window opens completely empty]] — same failure mode as the layout lessons, for the same root cause.

Creating a control and adding it to root.getChildren() are two separate steps, and skipping the second one is invisible at compile time — every control here is a perfectly valid object, [[key:it just never gets attached to anything the Scene actually renders]]. The broken version constructs a VBox and a handful of controls but never once calls getChildren().add() or addAll() on the VBox, so the Scene wraps a container that's technically there and visually empty.

phase3.openingDialogue: Controls — the building blocks of your UI! 🧱

mcq.question:
You create three RadioButtons for a "pick one" question but forget to call setToggleGroup() on any of them. What actually happens when a user clicks all three?

A) A compile error — RadioButtons require a ToggleGroup to be constructed
B) Only the first one stays selected, the rest are automatically deselected
C) All three stay selected at once, because nothing is enforcing exclusivity between them
D) A runtime exception the moment the second one is clicked

phase4.selfChallenge:
Write a JavaFX program that:
1. Creates a VBox with spacing 15 and padding 20
2. Adds a Label "User Registration"
3. Adds a TextField with prompt "Enter username"
4. Adds a TextField with prompt "Enter password" (use PasswordField)
5. Adds a CheckBox "Remember me"
6. Adds a ComboBox with "Student", "Teacher", "Staff"
7. Adds a Button "Register"
8. Shows the window

phase5.trivia: [[fun:TextField and TextArea both descend from a common TextInputControl class]], which is why prompt text, editability, and basic text-selection behavior work identically on both — TextArea just adds multi-line wrapping and a scrollbar on top of the same foundation.
